title: Tabersonine Alleviates Cerebral Ischemia/Reperfusion Injury Partly via Repressing the SLC6A2/NF-kappaB Signalling Pathway.
authors: Zhang, Li; Chen, Liji; Chen, Juhua; Ge, Xuehua; Yu, Yingchun; Sun, Panpan; Ruan, Yonglan
one_liner_zh: 该文研究Tabersonine通过SLC6A2/NF-kappaB通路缓解脑缺血再灌注损伤，仅用分子对接初步预测小分子-蛋白结合，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: The study aimed to investigate the neuroprotective functions and the underlying regulatory mechanisms of Tabersonine in cerebral ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury. Oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R)-treated neural cells were used as a cell model under I/R context. Cell counting kit 8 (CCK8) assay and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) were used to assess the cell viability and the release levels of inflammatory cytokines (interleukin-1beta (IL-1beta), IL-6 and tumour necrosis factor alpha (TNF-alpha)) of treated neural cells. The apoptotic proportions of treated neural cells were analysed by flow cytometry, and the intracellular levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and superoxide dismutase (SOD) were quantified by corresponding kits. In this study, molecular docking analysis identified solute carrier family 6 member 2 (SLC6A2) as a potential target of Tabersonine in cerebral infarction, demonstrating a high binding affinity of -7.4 kcal/mol. Tabersonine treatment increased neural cell viability, repressed apoptosis and reduced the release levels of IL-1beta, IL-6 and TNF-alpha under OGD/R stress. Moreover, Tabersonine treatment reduced ROS levels and increased SOD expression in neural cells under OGD/R treatment. In contrast to the protective effect of SLC6A2 knockdown, its overexpression counteracted the neuroprotection conferred by Tabersonine. Tabersonine also inactivated the NF-kappaB pathway partially via SLC6A2. Furthermore, Tabersonine pretreatment demonstrated significant neuroprotective effects in MCAO/R rats, as evidenced by reduced brain edema and attenuated neural inflammation and apoptosis. In conclusion, Tabersonine can alleviate neural impairment in cerebral I/R injury partially by inactivating the NF-kappaB pathway through SLC6A2.
abstract_zh: 本研究旨在探讨Tabersonine在脑缺血/再灌注（I/R）损伤中的神经保护功能及其潜在调控机制。采用氧糖剥夺/复氧（OGD/R）处理的神经细胞作为I/R背景下的细胞模型。使用细胞计数试剂盒8（CCK8）实验和酶联免疫吸附测定（ELISA）评估处理神经细胞的细胞活力及炎症细胞因子（白细胞介素-1β（IL-1β）、IL-6和肿瘤坏死因子α（TNF-α））的释放水平。通过流式细胞术分析处理神经细胞的凋亡比例，并使用相应试剂盒定量细胞内活性氧（ROS）和超氧化物歧化酶（SOD）水平。本研究中，分子对接分析确定溶质载体家族6成员2（SLC6A2）为Tabersonine在脑梗死中的潜在靶点，显示出-7.4 kcal/mol的高结合亲和力。Tabersonine处理在OGD/R应激下增加了神经细胞活力，抑制了凋亡，并降低了IL-1β、IL-6和TNF-α的释放水平。此外，Tabersonine处理在OGD/R条件下降低了神经细胞中的ROS水平并增加了SOD表达。与SLC6A2敲低的保护作用相反，其过表达抵消了Tabersonine赋予的神经保护作用。Tabersonine还部分通过SLC6A2失活了NF-κB通路。进一步地，Tabersonine预处理在MCAO/R大鼠中显示出显著的神经保护作用，表现为脑水肿减轻以及神经炎症和凋亡减弱。总之，Tabersonine可部分通过SLC6A2失活NF-κB通路，从而减轻脑I/R损伤中的神经损伤。
